lessons.title: Project, folders, and file-based routes
lessons.concept: In App Router, every folder under app is a potential segment and only page.tsx makes that segment publicly visitable. The components, lib, and public folders organize interface, shared logic, and static assets without automatically creating routes. First draw the inputs, transformations, trust boundaries, and outputs. That map lets you predict where code runs and where each failure must be handled.

Recognize failure states, read their symptoms, and apply a verifiable correction.

blocks.text: Special files surround a segment: loading.tsx is a fallback during suspension, error.tsx catches a rendering failure on the client, and not-found.tsx explains a missing resource. Every boundary should preserve context and provide a next action. First draw the inputs, transformations, trust boundaries, and outputs. That map lets you predict where code runs and where each failure must be handled.

blocks.title: Simple analogy
blocks.text: waiting and recovery boundaries is like a building where folders are floors, layouts are shared hallways, and page.tsx is the visited room. The analogy helps you remember the main journey, but running code is the evidence: inspect every value at the input, during transformation, and at the output.

A loading skeleton reserves final dimensions to prevent layout shift and announces waiting without fake progress. Start with the smallest working version and inspect its real value in the terminal or DevTools before adding an abstraction.

error.tsx must be a Client Component to offer reset; it displays a safe message and logs the cause without exposing a stack or secret. Then connect the rule to the contract between browser, server, and database; every boundary needs a defined input and an explicit failure.

The not-found page names what is missing and offers a relevant Link; browser back is insufficient for a directly shared URL. Finally test the normal case, a boundary input, and a deliberate failure so the behavior is proven beyond the happy path.
